By pure coincidence I was just writing what has become an essay on the state of differential geometry and what I have done in https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/37932 and https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/38374

Let me run it by you here before posting to the world (or at least the world on Lean Zulip)
But I am not sure if you read these messages so I will hold back for now.
Ah I seem to have replied on the wrong channel - my apologies

Message 1:
Background and motivation

I thought it might be useful to give an update on where I think differential geometry is in Lean from a personal perspective. From what I understand of blueprints, maybe we should have one for this subject area?

My motivation comes from wanting to formulate Einstein's equations without the usual "débauche d'indices" (Cartan: preface to Leçons sur la géométrie des espaces de Riemann, 1928) and then solve them (but that's a different story).

As a warmup to Einstein, I wanted to understand how the definition of a connection arises. I had previously used SageMath but it did not contain the more geometric formulation of a connection due to Ehresmann, and since I did not want to program in Python — having programmed in functional languages for the last 30 years — I thought Lean would suit my purposes.

To go into the details of the various formulations of connections would detract from my goal of summarising the state of differential geometry in Lean, but briefly: a connection can be defined in coordinates, with coefficients transforming as (see e.g. Carroll):

Γˉikl=∂xˉi∂xm∂xn∂xˉk∂xp∂xˉlΓmnp+∂2xm∂xˉk∂xˉl∂xˉi∂xm{\bar\Gamma^i}_{kl} = \frac{\partial \bar x^i}{\partial x^m}\frac{\partial x^n}{\partial \bar x^k}\frac{\partial x^p}{\partial \bar x^l}{\Gamma^m}_{np} + \frac{\partial^2 x^m}{\partial \bar x^k \partial \bar x^l}\frac{\partial \bar x^i}{\partial x^m}Γˉikl​=∂xm∂xˉi​∂xˉk∂xn​∂xˉl∂xp​Γmnp​+∂xˉk∂xˉl∂2xm​∂xm∂xˉi​

On the other hand, a connection can be defined as a horizontal subspace of a principal bundle — these horizontal spaces encoding parallel transport — and equivalently by a Lie-algebra-valued 1-form with certain properties.

I wrote a definition of a principal bundle as a PR and was challenged that definitions without accompanying theorems were not acceptable for Mathlib and fair enough. After a detour learning Mathlib's differential geometry foundations — defining the Möbius strip as a non-trivial bundle and proving existence of Riemannian metrics — I settled on showing that the transformation law above can be derived from the coordinate-free definition of a connection on a principal bundle. More concretely, the transformation law is an instance of the Yang–Mills / gauge-transformation law:

Ω′=g−1Ωg+g−1dg\Omega' = {g^{-1}}\Omega g + g^{-1}dgΩ′=g−1Ωg+g−1dg

Message 2:
State of differential geometry in Mathlib

Merged PRs

PR #30083 — local frames on a vector bundle. grunweg's PR provides Basis.localFrame: given a trivialisation of a vector bundle and a basis of the model fibre, it constructs a smooth local frame — a smoothly varying basis of the tangent spaces over an open set. This is the natural bridge between the abstract vector bundle structure and concrete index-based calculations, and is likely to be needed when the gauge transformation law is unpacked in coordinates to give the Christoffel transformation law.
PR #36234 — FiberBundle.extend. Patrick Massot, Michael Rothgang and Heather Macbeth provide a tool to extend an element of a fibre at a point to a local section of the bundle defined in a neighbourhood of the base point. This is the natural way to pass from a pointwise statement to a local statement about sections, and is likely to be needed when bridging from the abstract IsPrincipalBundle to the frame bundle — specifically when producing local sections of LMLMLM through a given frame in order to apply the gauge transformation law.
PR #36285 — torsion of an affine connection. grunweg defines the torsion tensor of an affine connection (a covariant derivative on TMTMTM) as T(X,Y)=∇XY−∇YX−[X,Y]T(X, Y) = \nabla_X Y - \nabla_Y X - [X, Y]T(X,Y)=∇X​Y−∇Y​X−[X,Y]. This definition is necessarily restricted to connections on $TM$: torsion measures the failure of parallelogram closure in the tangent bundle, and requires the connection to act on the same bundle whose sections appear as the arguments XXX and YYY. For a general vector bundle those two roles come apart and torsion is not defined. In the principal-bundle picture, torsion generalises to T=d∇θT = d^\nabla \thetaT=d∇θ where θ\thetaθ is the soldering form — a canonical Rn\mathbb{R}^nRn-valued 1-form on the frame bundle LMLMLM that identifies tangent vectors on MMM with vectors in the model fibre. Stating torsion in this picture requires both the soldering form and the exterior covariant derivative d∇d^\nablad∇, the latter depending on the manifold-level theory of differential forms that is currently a gap in Mathlib.
PR #35653 — quotients of charted spaces by free properly discontinuous group actions. Michael Rothgang, Archie Browne, Enrique Diaz Blanco, Juanjo Madrigal and Oliver Nash (an ItaLean 2025 project) add topological preliminaries for properly discontinuous group actions and equip the orbit space orbitRel.Quotient G M with a ChartedSpacestructure. The quotient map is shown to be a covering map and hence a local homeomorphism, and a ChartedSpaceinstance on the quotient is defined by composing local inverses with charts of $M$. Future PRs will upgrade this to a smooth manifold structure assuming a smooth action. This is the beginning of the quotient manifold machinery that the associated bundle construction requires: going from a connection 1-form on LMLMLM to a covariant derivative on TMTMTM is mediated by the associated bundle P×ρV:=(P×V)/GP \times_\rho V := (P \times V)/GP×ρ​V:=(P×V)/G, which needs exactly this smooth manifold quotient. For the immediate goal (the Christoffel transformation law) this can be sidestepped — see message 3 — but it will be needed for the longer-term development.
PR #29186 — IsIntegralCurve for ODEs on vector spaces. winstonyin defines integral curves for ODEs on vector spaces, paralleling the existing IsMIntegralCurve on manifolds. This is the analytic foundation that manifold-level flow results are built on: ODE results are proved first on Banach spaces and then lifted through charts. This PR is not used directly in the current development, but it underpins PRs #26394 and #34288 which together cover existence and smoothness of flows on manifolds — and once those are merged, they should discharge the contMDiff_flow_like axiom that the current development relies on.

PRs in progress

PR #26221 (Michael Rothgang) — covariant derivatives, Christoffel symbols, Levi–Civita. Develops connections, Christoffel symbols and the Levi–Civita connection on vector bundles directly, not via the principal-bundle route. Covers: smoothness of vector bundle sections; smooth local frames; a tensoriality criterion; covariant derivatives and their tensoriality; torsion-free connections; metric-compatible connections; definition and uniqueness of the Levi–Civita connection; Christoffel symbols. Existence of the Levi–Civita connection is still in progress. This is complementary to the principal-bundle development described in message 3. The Christoffel symbols defined there are the local connection coefficients of a covariant derivative on a vector bundle relative to a local frame — the same objects that appear in the transformation law I want to prove. The two approaches should agree.
PRs #26394 and #34288 — existence and smoothness of local flows on manifolds. These two in-progress PRs together cover Lee's Theorem 9.12 on joint smoothness of flows. PR #26394 (winstonyin) proves existence and continuity of local flows of a smooth vector field on a smooth manifold; PR #34288 proves smoothness of integral curves of ODEs on Banach spaces with respect to the initial condition, citing Lang's Fundamentals of Differential Geometry. Neither is used directly in the current development, but once both are merged, the contMDiff_flow_like axiom should be dischargeable by lifting through manifold charts.
PR #36299 (grunweg) — metric connections. Defines metric compatibility: a connection $\nabla$ on a Riemannian vector bundle (V,g)(V, g)(V,g) is compatible with the metric iff $\nabla g = 0$. There is active discussion on generalising the underlying RiemannianBundle typeclass to a MetricTensor abstraction covering indefinite (Lorentzian / pseudo-Riemannian) metrics, so that Lorentzian geometry can be developed without duplicating the Levi–Civita pipeline. This is directly on the path towards Einstein's equations.

Notable gaps

The most significant gap for the present project is differential forms on manifolds. Mathlib has differential forms on normed spaces (Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.DifferentialForm.Basic), including the exterior derivative and d2=0d^2 = 0d2=0. What is missing is the manifold-level theory: differential forms as smooth sections of ΛkT∗M\Lambda^k T^*MΛkT∗M, with pullback, wedge product, and integration. Without this, curvature F=dω+12[ω,ω]F = d\omega + \tfrac{1}{2}[\omega,\omega]F=dω+21​[ω,ω], the Bianchi identities, and the Yang–Mills field equation can't be stated. The Christoffel transformation law does not require this — it can be handled with mfderiv — but anything beyond it does.

Message 3:
Where I've got to

The code is a bit of a schlamassel, but I wanted to see how far I could get without some of the building blocks in place. And I feel quite (the English, not the American, version) pleased with the result.

What's built

Warmup: sections and forms. Before developing the principal bundle theory, I established that the pointwise pairing of a 1-form with a vector field is smooth (apply_smooth''). This is the basic instance of the machinery needed later for connection forms.

IsPrincipalBundle. A typeclass for a smooth principal GGG-bundle following Tu §27 / Bleecker §1.1, with GGG-equivariant local trivialisations as the primary condition. Transitivity of the GGG-action on fibres is proved as a theorem (IsPrincipalBundle.is_transitive) rather than assumed.
Connection 1-form and Yang–Mills transformation. The connection 1-form ConnectionForm is defined as a Lie-algebra-valued 1-form satisfying the two standard axioms (reproduces fundamental vector fields; equivariant under the right GGG-action). The gauge transformation law yangMills_transformation is proved:

ωU2(v)=Ad∗Ω−1(ωU1(v))+Ξ∗Ω(m)(dΩm(v))\omega^{U_2}(v) = \mathrm{Ad}*{\Omega^{-1}}(\omega^{U_1}(v)) + \Xi*{\Omega(m)}(d\Omega_m(v))ωU2​(v)=Ad∗Ω−1(ωU1​(v))+Ξ∗Ω(m)(dΩm​(v))

The proof goes via mfderiv_smul_section (the product rule for the derivative of $\sigma(x) \triangleleft \Omega(x)$) and mfderiv_action_at_g (which identifies the derivative of the right action with the fundamental vector field via the Maurer–Cartan form).
Fundamental vector fields. The fundamental vector field $$A^#$$ is defined, proved to be vertical (fundamentalVectorField_mem_vertical), proved to vanish only when A=0A = 0A=0 (fundamentalVectorField_zero_iff, using freeness of the action), and shown to generate integral curves (isMIntegralCurve_action_expLie). Smoothness as a section of the tangent bundle is also proved (contMDiff_fundamentalVectorField).
The frame bundle. The endomorphism bundle End(TM)≅Hom(E,TM)\mathrm{End}(TM) \cong \mathrm{Hom}(E, TM)End(TM)≅Hom(E,TM) is constructed as a VectorBundleCore, giving a smooth manifold structure on the total space for free. The frame bundle FrameBundle I M is then the open subset of invertible elements, inheriting its smooth manifold structure as an open submanifold. The right (E→LE)×(E \to_L E)^\times(E→L​E)×-action is defined, its smoothness proved (contMDiff_action), and freeness (frameBundle_action_isFree), fibrewise transitivity (frameBundle_action_isTransitive_val), and equivariance of trivialisations (frameBundle_triv_equivariant) are all established.

What's axiomatised

Two axioms remain, both of which should be dischargeable given work already in progress in Mathlib.
contMDiffAt_gaugeMap — smoothness of the gauge map between two local sections. This is axiomatised because equivariant_triv in IsPrincipalBundle is currently stated only for the canonical trivialisation trivializationAt, whereas the standard argument needs it for any atlas trivialisation. Generalising equivariant_triv would let this follow from Bundle.Trivialization.contMDiffOn_of_fiberBundle.
contMDiff_flow_like — joint smoothness of the flow of a smooth vector field (Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, Theorem 9.12). PRs #26394 and #34288 are converging on exactly this statement, and once both are merged the axiom should be dischargeable by lifting through manifold charts.

What's faked at the differential-forms level

The connection 1-form ω\omegaω and the Maurer–Cartan term g−1dgg^{-1}dgg−1dg are currently expressed via mfderiv rather than as genuine differential forms on a manifold. This is enough for yangMills_transformation and hence for the Christoffel transformation law, but it means that curvature F=dω+12[ω,ω]F = d\omega + \tfrac{1}{2}[\omega,\omega]F=dω+21​[ω,ω] and the Bianchi identities cannot currently be stated. All of these are gated on a Mathlib development of differential forms on manifolds as smooth sections of ΛkT∗M\Lambda^k T^*MΛkT∗M — the notable gap described in message 2.

What remains

The immediate gap is the bridge between the frame bundle and IsPrincipalBundle. The total space ↥(FrameBundle I M) is not in the Bundle.TotalSpace G E shape that IsPrincipalBundle expects, so yangMills_transformation cannot be applied to it directly. The most promising route is to restrict the trivialisations of EndBundle to invertible elements, obtaining trivialisations of the frame bundle in the right shape — if Mathlib has, or is willing to accept, machinery for restricting a FiberBundle to an open subbundle. Once that bridge is in place, specialising yangMills_transformation to the frame bundle and unpacking in coordinates — using the local frames from PR #30083 — should give the Christoffel transformation law.

For the longer term, going from the connection 1-form on LMLMLM to a covariant derivative on TMTMTM via the associated bundle construction P×ρV:=(P×V)/GP \times_\rho V := (P \times V)/GP×ρ​V:=(P×V)/G requires the smooth manifold quotient machinery that PR #35653 has begun. This can be sidestepped for the Christoffel transformation law — the induced connection on TMTMTM can be constructed directly in local frames — but the general theory will be needed eventually.
And the code is here: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/38374 and I will now change its name
